key_insight: Among the HVOF cermet coatings tested on 65G steel, WC–Co–Cr delivered the best overall performance by combining the densest microstructure, highest hardness, and lowest friction.
engineering_relevance: Powder composition and binder choice strongly control coating quality, making WC–Co–Cr the most promising option for components exposed to severe abrasive-adhesive wear.
method: HVOF spraying of WC–Co–Cr, WC–NiCr, WC–Ni, Cr3C2–NiCr, and Al2O3–NiCr coatings on 65G steel
Property evaluation using microhardness, surface roughness, tribology, and adhesive strength tests
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative comparisons across all coatings, with WC–Co–Cr achieving 1316.87 HV and μ = 0.143, while Al2O3–NiCr showed the lowest hardness (631.59 HV) and highest friction (0.630).
watch_item: Performance depends on spraying conditions and coating structure, so results may not transfer directly without process optimization for a specific HVOF setup.
paper_title: THE EFFECT OF THE COMPOSITION OF METAL-CERAMIC POWDERS ON THE STRUCTURE AND PERFORMANCE PROPERTIES OF COATINGS OBTAINED BY THE HVOF METHOD
